title: On the coefficient class the compact-support functor is computed on the étale site
statement:
Let $K_0$ be a field, let $X,Y$ be
finite-type
$K_0$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-pc-scheme], let $f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type
$K_0$-morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] with a
compactification [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]
$X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$, and fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$ of its ring of integers, and $n\geq1$. Put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension].
Write $Rf_{!,n}=Rp_*j_!$ for the pro-étale
compact-support functor
attached to that compactification, the extension by zero being the
pro-étale one and $Rp_*$ the
derived direct image, and write
$Rf_!^{\Et}=Rp_{\Et,*}j_!^{\Et}$ for the étale compact-support functor
attached to the same compactification, that of
[def-amb-etale-compact-support], its extension by zero being the
étale one and its proper
direct image $Rp_{\Et,*}$. Let $G\in\Dplus(X_{\Et},A)$ be a
bounded-below complex of $A$-module sheaves on $X_{\Et}$, and let
$K\in\Dplus(X_{\Proet},A)$ come from the étale site with
witness $(G,\alpha)$,
$\alpha:\nu_X^*G\xrightarrow{\sim}K$. Then the canonical comparison

$$
Rf_{!,n}K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\nu_Y^*\bigl(Rf_!^{\Et}G\bigr)
$$

is an isomorphism, natural in the witness. Here $\nu_T^*$ is the exact derived comparison pullback [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]; the derived module categories are [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] and [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], the witness is [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], pro-etale extension by zero is [def-weil-extension-by-zero], and pro-etale derived direct image is [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. All coefficient categories are ordinary constant-$A$ module categories.

proof.text: The coefficient construction [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] makes $A$ a finite commutative ring. The compactification [def-weil-compactifications-refinements] supplies an open immersion $j$ and a proper map $p$. By [pqf-lem-proper-basic], $p$ is quasi-compact, quasi-separated and of finite type. This checks the relative qcqs hypothesis; finite type alone is not being used to infer quasi-separatedness. To check the Noetherian hypothesis of [def-amb-etale-compact-support], observe that every ideal in the field $K_0$ is either zero or the whole field, so $\operatorname{Spec}K_0$ is locally Noetherian. Apply [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] to the structure maps of $X,Y$ and then to $p$ to get that $X,Y,\overline X$ are locally Noetherian. By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $X,Y$ have finite affine covers, hence are quasi-compact. Cover $Y$ by finitely many affine opens; their inverse images under the quasi-compact $p$ are quasi-compact and cover $\overline X$, so $\overline X$ is quasi-compact too. A finite subcover of locally Noetherian affine charts therefore makes all three schemes Noetherian. Thus the ordinary etale candidate in the statement is defined on this compactification.

source.place: Tags 01W1 (definition-proper), 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian); blueprint proof paragraph 1, fixed compactification and finite coefficients

proof.text: Write $A_T=\nu_T^*$ for [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]. The two open-extension functors are exact by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] and [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact]. By [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison], there is a specified natural sheaf isomorphism $e_{j,F}:A_{\overline X}j^{\mathrm{et}}_!F\to j^{\mathrm{proet}}_!A_XF$. For any complex $C$, naturality at its differential $d^r:C^r\to C^{r+1}$ says $e_{j,C^{r+1}}A_{\overline X}j^{\mathrm{et}}_!(d^r)=j^{\mathrm{proet}}_!A_X(d^r)e_{j,C^r}$. Thus its components, and their inverses, are chain maps. The exact functors induce the termwise derived functors by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]; since they preserve kernels and images, $H^r(F(C))=F(H^r(C))$, so they preserve quasi-isomorphisms and lower cohomological bounds. The natural isomorphism and its inverse descend along localization by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. We obtain the same specified natural isomorphism $e_{j,G}:A_{\overline X}j^{\mathrm{et}}_!G\xrightarrow{\sim}j^{\mathrm{proet}}_!A_XG$ in the bounded-below derived category, and $M=j^{\mathrm{et}}_!G$ belongs to $D^+(\overline X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$.

source.place: Tag 09AF (lemma-jshriek-comparison); sites-modules.tex Tag 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero-exact); derived.tex Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor); blueprint proof paragraphs 1-2

proof.text: We check the interpretation of the ordinary unbounded etale direct image in [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. The module category on $\overline X_{\mathrm{et}}$ has enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. For any $M\in D^+(\overline X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] supplies a bounded-below complex of injectives $I$ representing $M$, and states that $I$ is K-injective. The ordinary unbounded direct image of the etale candidate therefore takes $M$ to $Q(p_{\mathrm{et},*}I)$ by the K-injective computation in [def-amb-etale-compact-support], applied to the identity resolution of the representing complex $I$. The bounded-below right derived functor takes $M$ to exactly the same complex by [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective]. That complex is bounded below, since an additive direct image sends zero terms to zero. The identifications are natural: [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] represents any morphism between these K-injective models by its unique homotopy class, and both constructions send it to the homotopy class of the termwise direct image. Consequently the bounded-below comparison in the next step uses precisely $Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}$ of the ordinary candidate, not an independently chosen functor.

source.place: Tags 013K (lemma-injective-resolutions-exist), 070J (lemma-bounded-below-injectives-K-injective), 05TH (lemma-injective-acyclic), 05TI (lemma-enough-injectives-right-derived); blueprint proof paragraph 2, ordinary etale direct image

proof.text: Apply [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] to $u=p$ and $L=M=j^{\mathrm{et}}_!G$. Its hypotheses hold by steps 1-2. To fix the named map rather than only its endpoints, use [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]: $b_{p,M}:A_YRp_{\mathrm{et},*}M\to Rp_{\mathrm{proet},*}A_{\overline X}M$ is the transpose of $A_{\overline X}(\varepsilon^e_{p,M})\circ a_{p,Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}M}^{-1}$ under the derived pro-etale adjunction, where $a_p$ is that lemma's specified pullback comparison and $\varepsilon^e_p$ its etale counit. Its statement asserts that this particular $b_{p,M}$ is an isomorphism and is natural in $M$. Hence its inverse is the required direct-image leg $Rp_{\mathrm{proet},*}A_{\overline X}M\xrightarrow{\sim}A_YRp_{\mathrm{et},*}M$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, apply the qcqs direct-image comparison to the proper part; fixed counit-mate normalization from prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image proof paragraphs 1-2

proof.text:
The witness [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness] gives $\alpha:A_XG\xrightarrow{\sim}K$. Define the displayed canonical comparison explicitly as
$$c_{G,\alpha}=b_{p,M}^{-1}\circ Rp_{\mathrm{proet},*}(e_{j,G}^{-1})\circ Rp_{\mathrm{proet},*}j^{\mathrm{proet}}_!(\alpha^{-1}).$$
Its successive endpoints are $Rp_{\mathrm{proet},*}j^{\mathrm{proet}}_!K$, $Rp_{\mathrm{proet},*}j^{\mathrm{proet}}_!A_XG$, $Rp_{\mathrm{proet},*}A_{\overline X}M$, and $A_YRp_{\mathrm{et},*}M$. These are respectively $Rf_{!,n}K$ and $\nu_Y^*(Rf_!^{\mathrm{Et}}G)$ at the two ends, by the formulas in the statement and [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Each factor is an isomorphism: a functor sends inverse arrows to inverse arrows, and steps 2 and 4 provide the remaining inverses. Composition proves the assertion for the fixed compactification. No compactification-independence assertion is needed.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, witness identification, and paragraph 3, composition of the two comparisons

proof.text:
For completeness, naturality in the witness means the following. Let $(G',\alpha':A_XG'\xrightarrow{\sim}K')$ be another witness and let $g:G\to G'$ and $k:K\to K'$ satisfy $k\circ\alpha=\alpha'\circ A_X(g)$. Then $\alpha'^{-1}\circ k=A_X(g)\circ\alpha^{-1}$. Functoriality gives the naturality square for the first factor of $c$. Naturality of the descended $e_j$ in step 2 gives the square for the second factor, and naturality of the specified $b_p$ in step 4 gives the square for the third factor (the naturality equation for an isomorphism implies that for its inverse by multiplication by the inverse components). Composing these three squares gives
$$c_{G',\alpha'}\circ Rf_{!,n}(k)=\nu_Y^*(Rf_!^{\mathrm{Et}}(g))\circ c_{G,\alpha}.$$
This proves the requested witness naturality, including change of presentation by an isomorphism. For the zero complex the formula is the unique isomorphism between zero objects; the empty open is covered by the same exact functors. The argument uses neither constructibility nor a cohomological-dimension bound.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3, naturality in the witness made into its explicit commutative square
